attempts.label: DANDI:000632
attempts.paper_title: Control of the Electroporation Efficiency of Nanosecond Pulses by Swinging the Electric Field Vector Direction
attempts.entry_title: Co- and cross-directional paired nanosecond pulses in a square electrode array (Kim et al. 2023)
attempts.description: Tests the Figure 3 findings of Kim, Semenov, Kiester, Keppler, Ibey, Bixler, Colunga Biancatelli and Pakhomov (2023) on dandiset 000632, which holds one stitched whole-dish image (MemBrite and YO-PRO-1) for each of 24 BPAE monolayers exposed to four co- or cross-directional paired pulses at 1 Hz or 770 kHz. It measures YO-PRO-1 uptake in the 200 um ROI at the center of the array, with and without the electrode-footprint background, and compares the four groups by t-tests. The triangular-array and strobe-imaging experiments of Figures 2, 4 and 5 are not in the dandiset; they are in DANDI:000631, 000633 and 000634.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Kim et al. (2023), Figure 3, from dandiset 000632

outcomes.statement: At 1 Hz, co-directional and cross-directional (90 degree) paired pulses in the square array have the same electroporation efficiency, measured as YP uptake at the array center.
outcomes.quote: Consistently with the measurements in Figure 2 , co- and cross-directional pulses at 1 Hz had the same electroporation efficiency ( Figure 3 )
outcomes.notes: Under background reading (b) the co-directional dishes at 1 Hz (mean 665, n = 5) average 0.68 of the cross-directional ones (972, n = 6); two-tailed Student's t-test p = 0.32, so the test does not find a difference. Reading (a) gives ratio 0.75, p = 0.31; Welch's test and the variants (whole-disc footprint background, YP over MemBrite, center ROIs of 150 and 250 um, without dishes whose footprint centers are more than 400 um from a parallelogram, the deposit as labelled) give p from 0.28 to 0.68. By experiment day the comparison goes opposite ways, 0.45 on 2022-11-29 (p = 0.023, n = 3 and 3) and 1.43 on 2022-12-04 (p = 0.49, n = 2 and 3). The test has little power, so p >= 0.05 shows that no difference was found, not that the groups are equal. The 95% interval of the difference is -968 to 356 counts (co/cross 0.00 to 1.37), and the test would detect with 80% power only a difference of 922 counts, 95% of the cross-directional mean; at the observed difference (-306 counts, s.e. 293) its power is 16%. With the ROIs at the refined footprint centers the ratio is 0.72, p = 0.40.
deviations: The center ROI is placed automatically at the mean of the four electrode footprint centers, located by template matching on a reduced YP image (epimg.find_footprints); the paper placed it by hand in MetaMorph (Methods 4.4). The located footprints and ROI are shown for every dish. As a check the footprints are located again on a finer image (5.2 um blocks, epimg.refine_footprints); over the 23 distinct dishes the refined array center lies a median 55 um (6 to 193 um) from the one used, and placing the ROIs there is run as a variant with the same outcomes.

Assumption. The files give no pixel size. 0.65 um per pixel is assumed (the 6.5 um ORCA-Flash4 pixel behind the 10x objective named in Methods 4.4); under it the footprints measure a median 1.59 mm across against the 1.5 mm needles (Methods 4.2), and on the finer image a median 1.66 mm. If the footprints are 1.5 mm across, the true pixel is about 0.59 to 0.61 um and the 308-pixel center ROI covers about 180 to 190 um, smaller than the paper's 200 um. The 0.5 mm lumen cannot be seen in the images (YP inside it is 0.97 to 1.13 times the YP around it), so it gives no second check. Center ROIs of 150 and 250 um sides are run as variants and give the same outcomes.

Background reading (b) subtracts the mean YP of a 200 x 200 um ROI at the center of each of the four footprints. Methods 4.4 says only that measurements were made within the footprints 'to account for spontaneous YP uptake'; the ROI size is the paper's, its place a stated choice, and a variant over the whole disc inside 0.6 of the footprint radius gives the same outcome.

Assumption. The dataset holds 23 distinct dishes, not 24. The file labelled co-directional 1 Hz, sub-BPAE-8unipolar-1Hz-04, is a copy of the cross-directional 1 Hz file sub-BPAE-8bipolar-1Hz-600ns-04 and is counted once, as cross-directional (its start time is in the 2022-11-29 series, where number 04 is otherwise missing, and its anisotropy index is in the cross-directional range). The groups then have 5, 6, 5 and 7 dishes (co 1 Hz, cross 1 Hz, co 770 kHz, cross 770 kHz) against the paper's n = 6 each. The deposit as labelled is shown as a variant and gives the same outcome.

outcomes.statement: Raising the pulse frequency from 1 Hz to 770 kHz enhances electroporation by co-directional paired pulses, attributed to temporal summation of the induced membrane potential.
outcomes.quote: Increasing the pulse frequency to 770 kHz enhanced electroporation by the co-directional pulses because of the temporal summation of the induced membrane potential
outcomes.notes: The co-directional mean at 770 kHz is higher than at 1 Hz, 1.67-fold under reading (a) and 1.96-fold under reading (b) (1301 against 665, n = 5 and 5), but the two-tailed Student's t-test does not find the difference (p = 0.15 and 0.16). No variant reaches p < 0.05; the smallest p is 0.087 (YP over MemBrite). The two background readings agree, so the claim is not blocked. On 2022-11-29 the 770 kHz mean is 2.74 times the 1 Hz one (p = 0.060, n = 3 and 3), on 2022-12-04 0.76 times it (p = 0.47, n = 2 and 2). The 95% interval of the difference is -315 to 1586 counts (ratio 0.53 to 3.38), and the test would detect with 80% power only a difference of 1321 counts, 199% of the 1 Hz mean. If the observed difference (636 counts, s.e. 412) were the true one, the test would find it with a power of 27%. With the ROIs at the refined footprint centers the ratio is 1.66, p = 0.20. The temporal summation explanation is not tested.

outcomes.statement: Cross-directional paired pulses at 770 kHz are just as effective as at 1 Hz; charging two different regions of the membrane does not cause summation.
outcomes.quote: Interestingly, charging two different regions of the cell membrane did not cause summation, making cross-directional pulses at 770 kHz just as effective as at 1 Hz

outcomes.statement: At a 180 degree change of field direction, paired-pulse trains give less YP uptake than single-pulse trains, 2-fold less at 1 Hz and 20-fold less at 833 kHz.
outcomes.quote: Maximum cancellation was expectedly observed at the 180° vector change, reducing YP uptake compared to single-pulse trains 2-fold at 1 Hz and as much as 20-fold at 833 kHz
outcomes.notes: The claims file scopes this claim to DANDI:000632 (data dataset), which holds only the square-array experiment of Figure 3 (24 files, all labelled co- or cross-directional, 1 Hz or 770 kHz, and all showing a four-electrode square array). The Figure 2 recordings are public in DANDI:000631 (version 0.231012.1508, 15 assets, single- and paired-pulse trains at 1 Hz and 833 kHz), whose metadata name this paper as IsPublishedIn, although the paper's Data Availability Statement says the data are available on request. As the data are public, the block is not data_missing; the claim was not tested on 000631 because the claims file does not name it, and a reader is asked (questions/000632.yaml) whether to mark the claim data elsewhere. Even then it may stay blocked, as each ROI's angle comes from a field simulation the paper does not give.

findings.statement: One recording is deposited twice under two conditions. sub-BPAE-8unipolar-1Hz-04 (session Co-directional_1Hz) and sub-BPAE-8bipolar-1Hz-600ns-04 (session Cross-directional_1Hz) have identical chunk indexes, identical images and the same start time (2022-11-29 16:57). The start time and the image's pattern of uptake point to the cross-directional label, so the co-directional 1 Hz group holds 5 distinct dishes.

The group sizes do not match the paper. By label the files are 6 co-directional 1 Hz, 6 cross-directional 1 Hz, 5 co-directional 770 kHz and 7 cross-directional 770 kHz (5, 6, 5 and 7 with the copy counted once), where the paper's Figure 3 reports n = 6 for each group. The 2022-12-04 series has four cross-directional and two co-directional dishes at 770 kHz, and lacks a number 04. One cross-directional dish more and one co-directional dish fewer than the paper's n = 6 at 770 kHz would follow from one mislabelled dish, but the four cross-directional 770 kHz dishes of 2022-12-04, the day with the extra dish, have anisotropy indexes of 0.06 to 0.18, below every co-directional dish (0.31 to 0.75), so the labels are used as deposited.

The dandiset description and every session description say the electrodes were arranged in a triangular array. The images show four electrode footprints in a square, as the paper describes for this experiment (Methods 4.2, a 4-electrode square array).

The files give no pixel size (the ImageSeries has no resolution or field of view) and name the channels only in a free-text description. A scale of 0.65 um per pixel had to be inferred from the camera and objective; under it the electrode footprints measure 1.59 mm against the 1.5 mm needles.

The subject names carry undocumented tokens ('8bipolar', '8unipolar', '600ns'). 'bipolar' and 'unipolar' match the cross- and co-directional sessions, and '600ns' marks the files of 2022-11-29; the trailing numbers run 01 to 12 in order of start time within each day. None of this is described.

The dataset holds only the Figure 3 experiment. The data of Figures 2, 4 and 5 are in DANDI:000631, 000633 and 000634, whose metadata name the paper, but 000632 does not point to them, and the paper's Data Availability Statement says the data are available on request without naming any of the four dandisets.

Question for the paper's authors. Methods 4.4 says spontaneous YP uptake was measured within the electrode footprints but not where in the footprint, over what area, or how it entered the Figure 3 values (subtracted from the center ROI, or not). This attempt subtracts the mean of a 200 x 200 um ROI at the center of each footprint, and shows the raw values and a whole-disc variant; all give the same outcomes. Which pairs of groups the p-values printed in Figure 3 compare is also not stated in the text.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier tested find_footprints, _roi_mean, _disc_mean and ov_to_px on synthetic input, and checked the archive's other dandisets. It agreed with every outcome. Its main point was that the Figure 2, 4 and 5 data are public in DANDI:000631, 000633 and 000634, so the notebook's statement that they are not public elsewhere is false. It asked for each dish's center offset or a finer view of the center ROI, and for an independent check of the 0.65 um pixel size. In reply the revision locates the footprints again on a finer image, prints the offsets and shows the arrays at 10.4 um, runs the refined positions as a variant, prints the 95% interval and the smallest detectable difference for each test, lists the three other dandisets from the archive, changes the reason of the seven blocks to other, and asks a reader whether to mark those claims data elsewhere. The verifier also noted that the extra cross-directional and missing co-directional 770 kHz dish were not discussed; the notebook and the group-size finding now discuss them. entries.name: 000632-kim-2023
entries.title: Co- and cross-directional paired nanosecond pulses in a square electrode array (Kim et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the Figure 3 findings of Kim, Semenov, Kiester, Keppler, Ibey, Bixler, Colunga Biancatelli and Pakhomov (2023) on dandiset 000632, which holds one stitched whole-dish image (MemBrite and YO-PRO-1) for each of 24 BPAE monolayers exposed to four co- or cross-directional paired pulses at 1 Hz or 770 kHz. It measures YO-PRO-1 uptake in the 200 um ROI at the center of the array, with and without the electrode-footprint background, and compares the four groups by t-tests. The triangular-array and strobe-imaging experiments of Figures 2, 4 and 5 are not in the dandiset; they are in DANDI:000631, 000633 and 000634.
